findings.description: When n==0 the function returns start regardless of whether start falls on a weekend. According to the spec, if start is on Saturday or Sunday, the function should return the following Monday.
findings.evidence: candidate.add_business_days(date(2026, 11, 6), 0) returns date(2026, 11, 6) instead of date(2026, 11, 8).

findings.description: The arithmetic logic using weeks and extra incorrectly handles cases where the number of business days to add is a multiple of 5, producing an extra week. This causes the result to be one week late for such cases.
findings.evidence: candidate.add_business_days(date(2026, 11, 4), 5) returns date(2026, 11, 11) (Monday) instead of date(2026, 11, 9) (Friday) as specified.

review.summary: Candidate implementation violates the spec by incorrectly handling n==0 on weekends and by miscalculating the result when the number of business days to add is a multiple of 5.
